title: Heuristic session tethering and surge fallback for heterogeneous canaries
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: When performing canary or A/B rollouts that span regions and capacity tiers, rigid version pin semantics can cause either excessive user disruption (forced switch to a fallback variant mid-session) or overcommitment of scarce Dedicated capacity to maintain strict pinning. Goal: design a heuristic 'tether' that balances session stability, SLO adherence, and capacity elasticity during surge/failover events. The solution should support probabilistic canaries, cohort graduation, and deterministic escape for overloaded tiers while providing clear observability and operator controls.
acceptance_criteria: New tethering layer exists in the routing resolver that can attach a session affinity token with configurable TTL and decay policy
Router supports two escape behaviors: soft-eviction (graceful degrade to compatible variant) and hard-eviction (immediate re-route) configurable per rollout
Rollout controller can declare cohort graduation thresholds (latency/error budgets) which trigger automatic TTL shortening or cohort draining
Metrics emitted: tether_assigned, tether_evicted_reason, tether_ttl_remaining, tether_failover_count, cohort_graduation_rate
Operator console shows active tether counts per region/tier/model-version and exposes manual override to pin/unpin cohorts
design_notes: We propose a three-parameter tether: initial_ttl, decay_schedule (linear/exponential/step), and escape_policy (probabilistic, deterministic). On new session, routing resolver evaluates user affinity (cookie/session id/request token) and policy rules to decide whether to attach a tethered version token. During capacity surge or elevated latency, the orchestrator can shorten tethers for affected cohorts to accelerate drain. For probabilistic canaries, tethers are initially short and lengthen on positive signal (quality metrics), while for enterprise pinned sessions tethers default to long with conservative decay. The tether token is opaque but carries routing metadata (version id, cohort id, assigned_at). TTL shortening is done via control-plane push; clients receive updated sticky headers on next response edge. We avoid per-request DB lookups by encoding minimal state in the token plus a small LRU cache in the gateway for recently seen tethers.
tradeoffs_and_considerations: Encoding state in tokens reduces control-plane load but makes emergency revocation harder—we mitigate with short TTLs and a revocation bloom/AP cache for critical cases
Aggressive TTL shortening improves capacity reclaim but can increase error rate for heavy stateful sessions (long contexts). We recommend tiered policies per route (stateless vs stateful)
Probabilistic escape reduces blast radius but complicates observability—require instrumentation to correlate user requests with tether decisions
Private deployments need configuration knobs exposed in the on-prem control plane; defaults are conservative for enterprise customers
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Router shim that adds/reads tether tokens and enforces TTL locally (2 spikes, 1 week)
Phase 2: Control-plane API to push tether decay commands and cohort graduation thresholds (2 weeks)
Phase 3: Rollout controller integration to shorten/lengthen tethers based on metrics (2 weeks)
Phase 4: Console UX surfaces tether counts and manual override (design + front-end, 2 weeks)
Phase 5: Load test + chaos experiments to validate failover and eviction behavior (1 week)
Total: ~8 weeks (parallelization between infra, controller, and console teams)
risks: Revocation lag if many tokens are long-lived and control-plane messages are delayed
Complexity of deduplicating tether decisions across multi-region gateways
Misconfiguration could cause cohorts to get pin-locked and consume Dedicated capacity longer than intended
Telemetry explosion if every tether decision is emitted naively—need aggregated counters and sampling
qa_and_validation: Synthetic traffic experiments with mixed region/capacity constraints to measure failure and recovery paths
A/B test comparing current deterministic pin behavior vs tethered probabilistic policy across 1M requests
Fault injection: regional outage and sudden Dedicated pool eviction to observe escape behavior
E2E perf tests for token parsing overhead under 20k rps per gateway
